title: The Ultimate Contrarian Trade?
text:
The Ultimate Contrarian Trade?

Louis-Vincent Gave

Gavekal Research | 21 Oct 2026

French generals are said to spend their lives fighting the last war (i.e. the Maginot Line and all that…). The same could probably be said for European Union policymakers. Take the recent measures adopted by the EU to limit the sale of Chinese hybrid vehicles into Europe as an example (see The Cost Of Protection). On the face of it, this embrace of protectionist measures might seem to be in the “spirit of the age.” After all, today is supposed to be an age of “deglobalization” and of “great power rivalry”; an era of “reshoring” manufacturing production, and blocking of Chinese imports. However, how sustainable will such policies prove to be over the medium to long term?To answer this question, we will make like a Jesuit priest and answer with another question: specifically, what is likely to become the first concern of elected officials across most of the Western world in the coming months, quarters and years? Let me suggest this: it will be the rising cost of funding of government debt.
